preamble: Merger of the palatal implosive [ʄ] with the alveolar implosive [ɗ]. Ehret (1991) adds a Proto-Eastern Cushitic *ʄ (his *jʼ), which Sasse (1979) does not reconstruct. He argues it was an implosive because Yaaku keeps a palatal implosive and because, in all of Lowland East Cushitic, it fell together with PEC *ɗ. He treats this merger as one of the shared innovations that define Lowland East Cushitic. Arbore and Oromo keep the merged sound as ɗ. Afar and many Somali dialects carry it on to retroflex ɖ (see ʄ > ɖ). Burji, a Highland East Cushitic language, also has ɗ, which Ehret calls a mirror of the Lowland shift. Elsewhere in his correspondence table the reflexes differ: Sidamo sh [ʃ], Hadiya c, Yaaku j [ʄ], and Dullay š or (Saamakko) j. The change and its direction both depend on Ehret's reconstruction. Under Sasse's system these Lowland ɗ forms would simply continue *ɗ.
